fields.description:
Verify the one dependency we cannot check from outside before committing to the \~56h build.

Breakdown:

* Salesforce authentication plumbing, reused as-is by the build — 4h

* Direct-to-Drive upload probe, including whether Google permits browser-to-Google uploads from a Salesforce page (§4.2) — 5h

* Minimal test component and screen-flow embed check — 2h

* Test at realistic file sizes, document findings, recommend a path — 1h

EXIT CRITERIA

* GO: authentication reliable, upload and viewing work, an interrupted upload leaves no orphaned file behind, no blocking org policy, one path demonstrably sound. Proceed to build reusing the POC's auth work

* CONDITIONAL GO: works with a constraint worth weighing (e.g. a file-size ceiling). Report the constraint and its cost; WagerTech decides

* NO-GO: something blocks it, e.g. an org policy we cannot work around. Stop and report before further effort

Recommended architecture is Option B (browser sends direct to Drive) — removes a whole category of chunking code rather than adding it, and does not need revisiting if file sizes grow. Option A (Salesforce relays) is a known-good fallback since the existing Dropbox integration proves it works at current file sizes; would be sized from POC findings, not guessed now.

Blocked on WagerTech prerequisites C1-C7 (BUILD-94).

Source: Drive Storage doc §4.3, §6.

BILLING: SOW assumes native Salesforce storage, so this comes through as a change order. Client sign-off on the doc authorises the POC ONLY; the build is authorised separately after findings.
fields.summary: BUILD-93 — Google Drive proof storage: Proof of Concept (12h)

comments.body:
**APPROVED TO PROCEED — 2026-08-04. Client explicitly reprioritised this ahead of the CMS API work.**

Kobi had proposed tabling it \[47:22\]: "if this is not urgent, I would table this for later, and focus on deal and deal rep assignment and CMS API work first."

Joyce reversed that \[48:11\]: "if you were waiting on us for like the deal stuff and the GCP integration seems pretty straightforward, like folder structure aside, I would probably focus your efforts on the GCP while we're like 100% confirming stuff… internally on the deal side of things."

Emily signed off on the design \[52:00\]: "I think like what we've been talking around here, Kobi, then I think you're good."

**Not blocked on folder structure.** Agreed the POC proves file transfer and API calls first; folder hierarchy is iterative.

**Confirmed scope boundaries:**

* Target is **Google Drive via a service account**, not GCP proper. Kobi \[53:00\]: "what we're proposing here, it's Google Drive, essentially, through a service account where we're storing everything. Very similar to Dropbox."

* **No compression, no encryption** in scope — service-account security only.

* Files tagged by proof type on upload (sign-up / deposit / wager).

* Sign Up records keep the **link-paste** proof fields for Phase 1. Button-upload is the POC, not the Phase 1 UX.

**#1 requirement — per-rep walled garden.** Joyce \[43:14\]: "you should only have access and visibility over your own proofs… it's like a walled garden per rep", plus "a separate provision for like operations role to be able to see everything." Proposed hierarchy (not final): rep → player name → operator / sign up → date.

**Client-side dependencies:** service account provisioning is "an Alex thing" (Emily \[52:52\]). Emily also asked whether the required Drive permission scope is documented in the design doc — Kobi owes that: "It should. If not, I'll get that for you." \[54:14\]
